But netlist has different refs/values: C1,C2,C5,C8 100u; C3 0.1u; D1 PMEG3030EP; D3 SS54; J1/J10 Conn_01x03; J4 BAT; J5/J8 2x15; J7 Conn_01x04; J11 5V_POWER; Q2 IRLML6402; Q3 BC857; R1 2.2k; R3 0; R4 0; R6 20k; R8 10k; R10 2.2k; R13 1k; R15 2k; R16 1k; R17 5.1k; R19 0; R20 0; R21 47k; R22 0; R24 0; SW2 SPDT; U2 MAX3485. Missing R5? spec R5 47k, netlist R21 47k. Missing R2? R17 5.1k. Missing R7? R6 20k? Values maybe shifted.

Need detect anomaly. Could be component value/reference swaps? Need inspect connectivity.

First map spec intended to netlist refs (renumbered).
M-BUS connectors: J5 and J8 2x15. Servo headers: J1 and J10 1x03. BAT: J4. PortB: J7 1x04. 5V_POWER: J11 1x02. D1 in netlist PMEG3030EP (servo diode) and D3 SS54 (external 5V diode). Q2 P-MOSFET battery switch, Q3 PNP direction. U2 MAX3485.

Need check power:
+3V3 net: C3.1, J5.11, J8.11, Q3.2 E, R10.1, R15.1, R8.1, U2.8 VCC. Good. But Q3 emitter to +3V3? For PNP auto direction, emitter likely +3V3, collector drives DE/RE? Base via R17 from TXD2? Need check. R8 10k from +3V3 to /NET0011 (TXD2?) and R17 5.1k from /NET0011 to Q3 base. That is divider. OK.

+5V net: D1.2 A, D3.1 K, J5.27, J7.2, J8.27. D1 is servo diode? PMEG3030EP: anode to +5V, cathode to servo rail Net-(D1-K). D3 SS54: cathode to +5V, anode to J11.1 external 5V. So external 5V input J11 pin1 through D3 anode->cathode to +5V. Good. D1 from +5V to servo rail. Good.

Net-(D1-K): servo rail: C1.1, C2.2, C5.2, C8.2, D1.1 K, J1.2, J10.2. Good. Four 100u caps. Note C2 pin1 GND, pin2 servo. C5 pin1 GND, pin2 servo. C8 pin1 GND, pin2 servo. C1 pin1 servo, pin2 GND. OK.

GND: many. C3.2, U2.5, J7.1, J11.2, J4.2, J1.1, J10.1, J5.2,4,6, J8.2,4,6, R1.2, R6.2, SW2.3, C1.2, C2.1, C5.1, C8.1. Good.

Battery path: J4 BAT: pin1 to Q2.S, R21.2; pin2 GND. Q2 P-MOSFET IRLML6402: pin1 G, pin2 S, pin3 D. Net-(Q2-G): Q2.G, R21.1, SW2.B(pin2). SW2 pin3 C to GND, pin1 A unconnected. So switch between G and GND? For high-side P-FET: source battery positive, gate pulled low to turn on. R21 47k from gate to source (pull-up to battery positive) to keep off? Actually R21 between Q2.G and Q2.S (Net J4-Pin1). SW2 B to gate, C to GND. When switch closed, gate to GND, Vgs negative, P-FET on. When open, R21 pulls gate to source, off. Good. Q2.D to /NET0016, which connects J5.29/J8.29 bus BAT. Good.

External 5V: J11 5V_POWER: pin1 via D3.A, pin2 GND. Good.

PortB J7: pin1 GND, pin2 +5V, pin3 /NET0024 -> J5.9/J8.9, pin4 /NET0039 -> J5.3/J8.3. Spec J6 GND, +5V, two GPIOs passed through. OK.

Servo signal paths. Need map PWM/serial.
Spec: PWM mode: populate R3/R4 1k from PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin3/J8 pin3; R9-R12 0 select bus pins; R13/R14 0 bridge pin3 and MAX3485 TTL bus. Serial mode: R13/R14 short. In netlist refs: likely R16/R13? Let's inspect.

Servo J1: pin1 GND, pin2 servo rail, pin3 signal. J10: pin1 GND, pin2 servo rail, pin3 signal.

Net-(J1-Pin_3): J1.3, R16.1, R20.2.
Net-(J10-Pin_3): J10.3, R13.1, R20.1, R3.2.
/NET0017: R13.2, R19.1, R4.1.
/NET0030: R16.2, R22.1, R24.1.
/NET0025: R15.2, R3.1, U2.6 A.
/NET0026? U2.B: R1.1, R10.2, U2.7.

Bus nets:
/NET0015: J5.21/J8.21, R22.2.
/NET0028: J5.20/J8.20, R19.2.
/NET0027: J5.19/J8.19, R24.2.
/NET0021: J5.22/J8.22, R4.2.
So four 0 jumpers R22,R19,R24,R4 connect bus pins to servo signal nodes? Let's decode.

In spec R9-R12 0 select bus pins: pin 19/21 for ch1, pin20/22 for ch2. R13/R14 0 bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto MAX3485 TTL bus. In netlist there are R3/R4? Wait values: R3 0, R4 0, R13 1k, R16 1k, R19 0, R20 0, R22 0, R24 0.

Maybe intended: R16 and R13 are 1k series PWM resistors from bus-selected nodes to servo pin3? But netlist has R16 1k between /NET0030 and J1.pin3; R13 1k between J10.pin3 and /NET0017. R20 0 between J1.pin3 and J10.pin3 (bridges servo signal pins). R3 0 between /NET0025 (MAX3485 A?) and J10.pin3? Wait /NET0025 includes R15.2, R3.1, U2.6 A. R3 0 connects U2 A to J10.pin3. That seems wrong: MAX3485 differential line A connected directly to servo signal? In spec serial bus driven by MAX3485 TTL bus? Actually MAX3485 A/B differential lines maybe connected to servo signal? Need examine. For serial servos TTL serial? RS-485 transceiver A/B differential. But servo headers signal pin likely TTL serial? Wait spec: Serial mode: two servo signal pins bridged into one shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver. Hmm MAX3485 converts UART to differential RS-485/RS-422, not TTL. But serial servos might use TTL? Let's parse. U1 MAX3485: RO to RXD2? DI from TXD2? A/B to shared servo bus? In netlist: U2 RO pin1 to /NET0005 -> J5.16/J8.16 (RXD2). U2 DI pin4 to /NET0011 -> J5.15/J8.15, R17, R8 (TXD2). U2 A pin6 to /NET0025: R15 2k to +3V3, R3 0 to J10.pin3. U2 B pin7 to Net-(U2-B): R1 2.2k to GND, R10 2.2k to +3V3.

This looks like RS-485 differential lines A and B connected to servo signal pins? But J1 pin3 only via R20 to J10 pin3 and R16 to /NET0030. /NET0030 via R22/R24 to bus pins 21/19. J10 pin3 via R3 to U2.A. So if R3 0 populated, J10 signal pin is shorted to MAX3485 A. J1 signal pin is connected to J10 signal pin via R20 0, and to bus pins via R16 1k? Wait R16 is 1k between J1.pin3 and /NET0030. R13 is 1k between J10.pin3 and /NET0017. /NET0017 via R19/R4 to bus pins 20/22. So 1k series from bus pins to servo pins. But also R3 0 from J10.pin3 to U2.A, R20 0 from J1.pin3 to J10.pin3. This merges both servo signal pins and U2.A into one node. But what about U2.B? It is biased to +3V3/GND with 2.2k/2.2k? That is not connected to servo bus. For RS-485 differential, both A and B should connect to two-wire bus. Here only A connected to servo signal, B left as differential bias? That seems odd. Maybe the design uses MAX3485 as level shifter/inverter? Let's investigate.

Spec says R6,R7,R8,R15 bias/pull network on MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line. R6 2k, R7 20k, R8 2.2k, R15 2.2k. In netlist: R1 2.2k from U2.B to GND, R10 2.2k from U2.B to +3V3, R15 2k from +3V3 to U2.A, R6 20k from Q3.C/DE/RE to GND? Wait R6 20k between Net-(Q3-C) and GND, not A/B. Spec R7 maybe 20k on DE/RE? It says R6,R7,R8,R15 2k,20k,2.2k,2.2k bias/pull on A/B and DE/RE. Netlist values: R15 2k A pull-up; R1 2.2k B pull-down; R10 2.2k B pull-up? That creates common-mode bias? R6 20k pull-down on DE/RE. R8 10k pull-up on TXD2? Hmm.

Maybe actual design uses MAX3485 A line as single-ended TTL? Let's reason: Serial servos (RS304MD) likely use single-wire TTL serial, not RS-485 differential? But MAX3485 is RS-485 transceiver. It can be used as inverter? The A/B differential lines: If B is biased with pull-up/pull-down, A connected to servo signal, maybe it converts differential? Actually RS-485 transceiver receiver output RO is based on A-B differential. Driver output A/B when enabled. For half-duplex two-wire, both A and B connect to bus. If only A connected to servo signal and B is biased, not a proper differential bus. But maybe the servo signal is single-ended and B is used as bias/reference? Need not be anomaly if spec inferred? Spec says "shared single-wire TTL serial bus, driven by U1 (MAX3485)". But MAX3485 cannot drive TTL single-wire; A/B differential. However spec may be inaccurate? It says serial servos share signal line. Could be they use MAX3485 as 3.3V to 5V? Hmm.

Need find clear anomaly from files. Let's compare spec component values and netlist values. There are many reference shifts. Could be deliberate tampering: wrong resistor values swapped? Need identify one that changes behavior.

Spec: R3, R4 1k each series from PWM GPIO nets to servo pin3. Netlist has R13 and R16 1k, but also R3 and R4 0. Spec R13,R14 0 jumpers bridge J3/J8 pin3 and MAX3485 TTL bus. Netlist has R3 0 from U2.A to J10.pin3, R20 0 from J1.pin3 to J10.pin3. R4 0 from J10.pin3? Wait R4 0 between /NET0017 and /NET0021 (bus pin22). That is a 0 jumper selecting bus pin, not bridge. R19 0 between /NET0017 and bus pin20. R22/R24 0 between /NET0030 and bus pins 21/19. So the 0 jumpers are R3,R4,R19,R20,R22,R24? There are six 0 ohm jumpers, spec has R9-R12 four 0 for bus selection and R13/R14 two 0 for serial bridge = six. So mapping: bus selection jumpers: R19,R22,R24,R4? serial bridge: R20 and R3? But R3 is 0 from U2.A to J10.pin3, not from J10.pin3 to J1.pin3? R20 bridges J1/J10. So serial mode: R20 short (bridge servo pins), R3 short (connect U2.A to bus). OK. But spec says R13/R14 bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto MAX3485 TTL bus. It could be two jumpers: one between servo pins, one between one servo pin and transceiver. So R20 and R3 plausible.

But R13/R16 1k series PWM: R16 from /NET0030 to J1.pin3; R13 from /NET0017 to J10.pin3. OK.

Now issue: In netlist, R3 value 0 (not 1k), R13 value 1k. Spec says R3/R4 1k, R13/R14 0. If references exactly as spec, netlist would have wrong values swapped: R3 should be 1k but is 0; R4 should be 1k but is 0; R13 should be 0 but is 1k. But references are renumbered, so cannot compare directly. Need infer from topology: 1k series should be between bus selection node and servo pin. In netlist, R13 and R16 are 1k, located between bus selection nodes /NET0017 and /NET0030 and servo pins J10/J1. Good. R3 is 0 located between MAX3485 A and servo pin J10. That is serial bridge. So references not spec; no anomaly solely due to reference renumbering. Need judge design files for build, not exact refs? The spec component table uses reference designators but netlist has different refs. It may be a different revision with renumbering. We should map by function. But if netlist has R3/R4 as 0 and R13/R16 as 1k, likely intentional. Need not report as wrong values unless topology inconsistent.

Need inspect MAX3485 differential bias. Spec: R6,R7,R8,R15 2k,20k,2.2k,2.2k. Netlist: R1 2.2k, R6 20k, R8 10k, R10 2.2k, R15 2k, R17 5.1k, R21 47k. Missing 2.2k? There are two 2.2k R1/R10 on B line; one 2k R15 on A; one 20k R6 on DE/RE; one 10k R8 on TXD2; one 5.1k R17 base; 47k R21 gate. Spec R1/R2 10k/5.1k, R6/R7/R8/R15 2k/20k/2.2k/2.2k. Netlist has R8 10k, R17 5.1k, R15 2k, R6 20k, R1/R10 2.2k. OK.

But check Q2 BC857 (netlist Q3) topology. Spec: Q2 PNP driven from TXD2 via R1 10k, R2 5.1k to toggle DE/RE. Netlist: Q3 emitter +3V3, base via R17 5.1k to /NET0011 (TXD2), R8 10k from +3V3 to /NET0011. Collector to U2 DE/RE and R6 20k to GND. When TXD2 low, base pulled low via R17, PNP on, collector pulls DE/RE high? Wait PNP emitter +3V3, collector to DE/RE with pull-down R6 to GND. When base low, transistor conducts, collector near +3V3, DE/RE high => driver enabled/receiver disabled? DE high enable driver, /RE high disable receiver. When TXD2 high, base high, transistor off, R6 pulls DE/RE low => receiver enabled. Standard. Good.

Now potential anomaly: U2 A line connected to servo signal via R3 0, but U2 B line not connected to servo signal. In RS-485 half-duplex, both A and B should be connected to the bus. But maybe serial servo uses single-wire TTL and MAX3485 is used as open-collector? Need examine: If only A connected, B biased with pull-up/pull-down, differential receiver may still respond to A vs B. Driver will drive A and B differentially.
